page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2gne.2xlarge belongs to the Local SSDs server family, tailored for I/O-intensive workloads requiring direct-attached high-speed storage. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for AVX and AVX-512 instructions. Memory capacity is provisioned at 32.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles 959 GB of local SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. No hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark evaluations highlight modest compute and memory performance alongside capable caching behavior. Synthetic CPU stress tests reveal lower-tier throughput, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1107.29 and multi-core reaching 5872.27. Similarly, Geekbench scores of 938.0 in single-core and 3572.0 in multi-core place the instance in the bottom quartile for modern compute tasks. PassMark CPU overall scoring is within the median band at 6917.37, supported by AVX instructions delivering 5854.7 in extended instruction testing. Data compression benchmarks reflect this computational profile, showing single-threaded gzip compression at 19.08 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.21 GB/sec. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 38.93 GB/sec, whereas write bandwidth hits 35.92 GB/sec. In key-value benchmarks, the server processed 6.1 million Redis SET operations per second, representing average performance among peer instances.

The primary value proposition of the ecs.i2gne.2xlarge lies in its direct-attached 959 GB SSD storage combined with dedicated CPU threads, making it a viable configuration where storage proximity reduces latency without demanding premium compute speed. The 2 Gbps network ceiling and older processor microarchitecture represent clear tradeoffs, making it less suitable for high-throughput network streaming, complex distributed builds, or intensive machine learning model inference. However, the balance of dedicated vCPUs, 32 GB memory, and high-capacity local SSD creates a practical hardware profile for transactional relational databases, NoSQL data stores, caching nodes, and localized ETL pipelines.

The instance integrates 959 GB of dedicated local SSD storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, operating without GPU acceleration. Benchmark results indicate modest CPU execution, recording 938.0 on single-core and 3572.0 on multi-core Geekbench suites, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 6917.37.
